tfn.s: Pauline's grandson helped to organise the adventure.
tfn.why: The text says: "Her grandson, Ross Smith, had helped organise the adventure."

tfn.s: Pauline stayed lying down until the end of the concert.
tfn.why: The text says: "When she reached the front, she stood up and enjoyed the moment on stage."

tfn.s: Ross also tried crowd-surfing at the concert.
tfn.why: The text does not say that Ross crowd-surfed.

tfn.s: Pauline enjoyed the ride from the very first second.
tfn.why: The text says: "At first she held on tightly. Then... she relaxed and started to enjoy herself."

tfn.s: Ross and Pauline made videos together before the record attempt.
tfn.why: The text says that years earlier Ross filmed his grandmother and "They carried on making videos together".

focus.note: A collocation is a pair of words that often go together. Learn the pair as one piece: break a record, pay attention.

items.s: Many athletes train for years to ____ a world record.
Pauline did not wait for a perfect age to ____ an adventure.

My grandfather has a wonderful sense of ____.
Seeing the northern lights for the first time was truly ____.
The course was ____ difficult, but it got easier after a few weeks.
Language can be a ____ when you move to a new country.
It is a false ____ that you have to be young to learn a language.

tfn.s: Ross and Pauline's partnership began before the record attempt.
tfn.why: The text says their partnership "began years earlier when Ross filmed Pauline blocking one of his basketball shots".

tfn.s: Pauline felt confident from the moment she was lifted.
tfn.why: The text says she held tightly at first and became more confident once she saw how carefully the crowd supported her.

tfn.s: Pauline practised being passed over a crowd before the concert.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether Pauline practised.

tfn.s: The writer thinks the story challenges an idea about later life.
tfn.why: The text says it "challenges the expectation that later life must always be quiet and predictable".

tfn.s: The writer says that everyone should try extreme activities.
tfn.why: The text says: "Pauline's example does not mean everyone should take up extreme activities."

focus.note: Collocations are word partners that sound natural together. Try the pair in your head: you build an audience and share memories, but you do not make memories shared.

items.s: Over many years, the chef managed to ____ a restaurant that everyone in town loved.
At the party, the old friends began to ____ memories of their school days.
A funny story can ____ even a tired person laugh.
She has a warm ____ and makes friends easily.
Skydiving and bungee jumping are ____ sports.
The wedding speech seemed ____, but the groom had in fact rehearsed it for weeks.
She trained as a nurse and ____ became head of a large hospital.
Many films avoid ____ older characters as helpless or unhappy.

tfn.s: The basketball clip came before the idea of a Guinness title.
tfn.why: The clip was filmed "years earlier"; the Guinness idea came later, when Ross "came up with" it.

tfn.s: Pauline was already a hundred years old when she crowd-surfed.
tfn.why: She was ninety-nine years and 274 days old; she had celebrated her hundredth birthday by October 2026.

tfn.s: Pauline wore her T-shirt because Ross asked her to.
tfn.why: The text says what the T-shirt celebrated but not why she chose it.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that ageing is often described in negative terms.
tfn.why: The text says later life is "frequently described in terms of decline, dependence and things that can no longer be done".

tfn.s: The writer believes the difficulties of ageing should be ignored.
tfn.why: The text says: "Those realities matter, but they do not account for the whole person."

focus.note: At C1, many collocations are formal verb and noun pairs: strike a balance, pose a risk. Check the noun first, then choose the verb that fits formal writing.

items.s: Campaigners hope the documentary will ____ outdated stereotypes about old age.
The council must strike a ____ between safety and freedom.
The announcement is likely to ____ fierce debate among voters.
Such a stunt would ____ a serious risk to untrained participants.
The charity runs a campaign to raise ____ of loneliness among older people.

speak.title: Role-play: a special day out for Gran
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want to take your grandmother, who is eighty-five, to a live concert. She has said she would love to go. Explain your plan and answer your parent's worries.

b.text: You love your mother, but you are worried that a noisy concert will be too tiring. Ask at least two questions. You can say yes, no, or yes with a condition.

phrases: I'd like to take Gran to a live concert.
I'm worried it'll be too tiring for her.
Let's ask her what she wants.
How about we book seats near the exit?
I'm sure she'll be fine if we plan it carefully.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the parent agree, and what condition made the plan safe?
